summary:
ASTRA CARE is a personalized health monitoring platform designed to support astronauts before, during, and throughout long-duration space missions.

The idea behind ASTRA CARE is simple: an astronaut's health should not be monitored only after a problem appears. Their health journey should be understood from the beginning. Before a mission, astronauts can create a personal health profile by providing their medical history, previous health check-up results, existing health conditions, and medication details.

During the mission, they can regularly record health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, oxygen levels, sleep, and mood. The platform compares these updates with their pre-mission health information, highlights important changes, and provides personalized health guidance, nutrition suggestions, medication reminders, and rest recommendations.

If a potentially serious health concern is identified, ASTRA CARE can help notify the relevant medical team and designated crew members. The aim is to make health information easier to understand and help astronauts take a more informed and proactive approach to their well-being in space.
details:
ASTRA CARE – Detailed Project Description

1. Background and Problem

Space missions expose astronauts to conditions that are very different from life on Earth. Altered gravity, space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, and the hostile environment of space can affect both physical and mental health.

During long-duration missions, even small changes in an astronaut's health may become important if they are not noticed early. Access to medical support can also be challenging when astronauts are far away from Earth.

Every astronaut has a different health background. Their previous medical conditions, nutritional needs, medication requirements, and physical condition may influence how they respond to the space environment. Therefore, a health monitoring system should consider not only their current readings but also their individual health history.

2. Our Proposed Solution

ASTRA CARE is designed as a personal health assessment and monitoring platform that follows an astronaut's health journey from pre-mission preparation to the end of the mission.

Instead of looking at every astronaut in the same way, the platform uses individual health information as a reference. It helps astronauts record their health data, understand changes over time, and receive relevant guidance.

3. Main Features

A. Pre-Mission Registration and Health Profile

Before travelling to space, each astronaut can register and create a personal health profile. This profile may include:

- Previous medical history and existing health conditions.

- Blood pressure, blood glucose, cholesterol, and other relevant health check-up results.

- Heart rate, body temperature, and oxygen saturation.

- Current medications and prescribed dosage schedules.

- Allergies, dietary restrictions, and nutritional requirements.

This information creates a personal health reference that can be used during the mission.

B. Personalized Nutrition and Food Planning

Based on the astronaut's health profile and nutritional requirements, ASTRA CARE can support the preparation of a personalized food and nutrition plan before the mission.

The plan can consider existing health conditions, nutritional requirements, dietary restrictions, and the food supplies available for the mission. This can help the medical and mission teams plan suitable food requirements in advance.

C. In-Space Health Monitoring

During the mission, astronauts can enter their health information through daily or weekly check-ins.

The platform can include fields for:

- Heart rate.

- Blood pressure.

- Blood glucose.

- Body temperature.

- Blood oxygen level.

- Sleep duration and quality.

- Mood, stress, and general well-being.

- Other relevant health observations.

The recorded information can be compared with the astronaut's pre-mission health profile to highlight changes that may need attention.

D. Health Trends and Early Warnings

ASTRA CARE presents health information through a visual dashboard so astronauts can understand their health status more easily.

It can highlight measurements that may be outside the expected range, display changes over time, and provide alerts when an entry requires attention.

The platform can also identify possible nutritional concerns from the available information and suggest that the astronaut seek medical review when necessary.

E. Medication Reminders

Astronauts may need to follow different medication schedules during a mission. ASTRA CARE can provide reminders based on the medication plan prescribed and approved by their medical team.

It is intended to support medication adherence, not independently prescribe medicines or change their dosage.

F. Medical Alert and Communication System

When the recorded information indicates a potentially serious health concern, the system can generate an alert for the appropriate medical personnel.

Depending on the mission communication setup, alerts may be shared with:

- The astronaut's designated doctor on Earth.

- The mission medical team.

- Relevant mission control personnel.

- Designated crew members when necessary.

This feature is intended to support timely communication and medical attention.

G. Rest and Mental Wellness Support

Physical health is only one part of an astronaut's overall well-being. Isolation, confinement, workload, and changes in the space environment can also affect mental health.

ASTRA CARE includes check-ins for mood, stress, sleep, and fatigue. Based on the recorded information, it can provide reminders and preventive suggestions related to rest, sleep routines, and mental wellness.

When repeated concerns are noticed, the platform can encourage the astronaut to contact the appropriate medical or psychological support team.

4. Connection with the Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight

ASTRA CARE is designed with NASA's five major hazards of human spaceflight in mind:

- Space Radiation: Health records can be considered alongside available radiation exposure information.

- Isolation and Confinement: Mood, stress, sleep, and mental wellness can be monitored through regular check-ins.

- Distance from Earth: Health summaries and alerts can support communication with Earth-based medical teams.

- Altered Gravity: Changes in physical health and relevant health indicators can be tracked over time.

- Hostile and Closed Environments: Nutrition, sleep, general health, and other wellness indicators can be monitored during the mission.

5. How the Platform Works

1. The astronaut registers and creates a personal account.

2. Previous health information and medical check-up results are entered.

3. A personal health profile is created from the available information.

4. The platform supports preparation of a personalized nutrition plan.

5. During the mission, the astronaut records health information regularly.

6. New entries are compared with the pre-mission reference data and previous records.

7. The dashboard displays health trends, reminders, and alerts.

8. Potentially serious concerns are communicated to the designated medical team through the available communication system.

6. Expected Impact

ASTRA CARE aims to make personal health information easier to access and understand during long-duration space missions. By connecting pre-mission health history with regular in-space check-ins, it can help astronauts and medical teams notice changes, follow preventive guidance, and communicate health concerns more effectively.

The broader goal is to encourage a more personalized and proactive approach to astronaut health management.

7. Future Improvements

Future versions could include wearable-device integration, automatic collection of health measurements, secure sharing with authorized medical teams, offline access, more detailed health trend analysis, and integration with validated medical protocols.

8. Limitations and Safety

ASTRA CARE is an educational prototype and is not a certified medical device or a NASA-approved clinical system. Its alerts and screening rules are intended to demonstrate how health information could be organized and reviewed. They are not validated medical thresholds or diagnoses.

The platform does not independently prescribe medicines, modify treatment, or replace professional medical advice. Any real mission use would require medical validation, appropriate privacy and security measures, and approval from the relevant spaceflight medical authorities.
projectRefs: Bio-Monitor: Keeping an eye on astronauts' vital signs
